summary: Tested Report Lock feature (signed_off meetings). All 14 backend tests pass (100%). All 8 frontend requirements verified via Playwright. Feature works correctly.

minor.issue: Backend does NOT prevent self-approval: if requester is also listed as an attendee (e.g. Jane is both manager and in attendees list), she can approve her own reopen request. The frontend correctly blocks this with `&& !isReopenRequester`, but backend has no such guard.

action_items: Add self-approval guard to approve-reopen endpoint: if user_id == requester_id AND is_attendee, still block approval (must be a DIFFERENT user). Currently frontend blocks this but backend allows it.
critical_code_review_comments: approve_reopen (review.py:1852): Backend only checks `is_attendee OR is_different_manager` but does NOT exclude the requester from the attendee check. If requester is also an attendee, they can self-approve, bypassing the mutual consent intent.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Meeting 6a46da6d1936c45e856ce791 is signed_off. Report Lock feature fully tested: all locks (409) and allowed operations (200) verified. Reopen flow tested end-to-end. Only bug found: backend allows self-approval in approve-reopen when requester is also an attendee. Frontend blocks it correctly but backend should too.

rca_of_issue.root_cause: approve_reopen endpoint checks `is_attendee` without excluding the requester. Since Jane (manager/requester) is also listed in meeting.attendees, is_attendee=True, allowing self-approval.
rca_of_issue.reproduction: 1. Request reopen as jane (requester). 2. Call approve-reopen as jane (attendee). Backend returns 200.
rca_of_issue.mitigation: Add `and user_id != requester_id` to the is_attendee check: `is_attendee = user_id in attendee_ids and user_id != requester_id`
